report.incidentSummary: On Monday 2026-09-28 at market open (09:15 IST / 03:45 UTC), stock orders failed at an elevated error rate of ~17.5% across /v1/orders on order-service. While the on-call SRE initially suspected an external broker outage or throttling similar to past incidents PIR-2006 and PIR-2018, investigation of broker-connector showed nominal error rates (<0.4%) and healthy upstream latencies. The failures were directly caused by configuration change CHG-48221 applied on Friday 2026-09-25, which reduced order-service's HTTP client connection pool to broker-connector from 200 to 20 connections per host. During the Monday market open order surge, this client connection pool became fully saturated (20/20 busy), throwing 503 timeouts on 423 order placement requests between 03:45 UTC and 04:19 UTC.
report.rootCauseStatement: Configuration change CHG-48221 executed on 2026-09-25T13:00:00Z reduced order-service's broker_client.max_connections_per_host from 200 to 20. During the first subsequent market open surge on Monday 2026-09-28 at 03:45 UTC (09:15 IST), concurrent order volume overwhelmed the constrained 20-connection pool, causing 423 HTTP 503 errors with 'timed out waiting for a connection to broker-connector (client pool 20/20 busy)' until order traffic subsided around 04:19 UTC.

hypotheses.cause: Configuration change CHG-48221 reduced order-service's outgoing HTTP client connection pool to broker-connector from 200 to 20, causing connection pool exhaustion and 503 timeouts during the Monday market open order surge.
hypotheses.rationale: Directly evidenced by change record CHG-48221 modifying broker_client.max_connections_per_host from 200 to 20, dependency metadata indicating a 20-connection cap, order-service error rate jumping from ~0.4% to ~17.5% at 03:46 UTC, and 423 explicit error logs stating 'timed out waiting for a connection to broker-connector (client pool 20/20 busy)'.

hypotheses.cause: External broker API degradation or rate limiting throttled order placement during the opening auction, mirroring past incidents PIR-2006 and PIR-2018.
hypotheses.rationale: broker-connector showed no matching degradation: error rates remained below 0.38%, rate_limited_count was flat at 0-2/min, retry counts peaked at only 8/min, p95 upstream order latency peaked at 218.5 ms, and no order errors were recorded in broker-connector logs.

facts.statement: On Friday 2026-09-25T13:00:00.000Z, configuration change CHG-48221 reduced broker_client.max_connections_per_host on order-service from 200 to 20.
order-service error_rate surged from baseline (~0.35%-0.5%) to ~17.4%-17.65% beginning at 03:46 UTC (09:16 IST) and remained elevated until returning to baseline at 04:19 UTC.

Between 2026-09-28T03:45:02Z and 2026-09-28T04:18:59Z, order-service logged 423 status 503 ERROR entries on /v1/orders stating 'order <ref> failed: timed out waiting for a connection to broker-connector (client pool 20/20 busy)'.
broker-connector error rate remained under 0.38% (mean 0.21%), rate_limited_count averaged 0.225/min (max 2/min), retry_count peaked at 8/min, and p95 upstream latency on orders peaked at 218.5 ms.
order-service database pool wait time peaked at 5.57 ms (mean 3.03 ms) and CPU utilization peaked at 65.97% at 03:45 UTC, remaining below saturation.
Database metrics showed active connections of ~175.5, lock wait times under 4.5 ms, slow queries under 7/min, and CPU utilization of ~36% around 03:45 UTC.

inferences.statement: Market open on Monday 2026-09-28 at 09:15 IST (03:45 UTC) was the first high-concurrency order placement burst experienced by order-service since connection limits were reduced tenfold by CHG-48221 on Friday after market close.
The reporter's hypothesis of an external broker API outage or throttling (PIR-2006 / PIR-2018) was disproven by broker-connector's healthy upstream metrics and logs.

Internal order-service resources (CPU and database connections) and database infrastructure were not bottlenecked; failures were exclusively caused by client pool starvation between order-service and broker-connector.

assumptions.statement: Normal market open trading volume on Monday mornings requires significantly more than 20 concurrent downstream connections to broker-connector to handle order concurrency without queue timeouts.

timeline.event: Change CHG-48221 is applied after market close, reducing order-service's broker_client.max_connections_per_host from 200 to 20.
Indian equity markets open. Influx of stock order placements begins hitting order-service.
order-service logs the first 503 error due to connection pool exhaustion ('client pool 20/20 busy').
order-service error rate spikes to ~17.4%, peaking at 17.65% at 03:49 UTC.
Last 503 error logged for broker-connector client pool timeout as morning burst order volume subsides.
order-service error rate recovers to baseline (0.35%).

confidence.rationale: High confidence supported by explicit error logs naming the exact pool size constraint (20/20 busy), an exact matching config change CHG-48221 lowering pool size from 200 to 20, and clear disproof of broker degradation via broker-connector metrics and logs.

gaps.description: Latency metrics (latency_p50_ms, latency_p95_ms) and route-specific error rates on api-gateway were not queried due to specialist task budget limits.
gaps.impact: Minimal impact; order-service logs and service-level error rate metrics provided direct evidence of order failure counts, status codes, and pool saturation.

recommendedActions.action: Revert or increase broker_client.max_connections_per_host in order-service configuration from 20 back to at least 200 (or higher as dictated by peak capacity modeling).
recommendedActions.rationale: Restores sufficient client connection concurrency between order-service and broker-connector, preventing connection pool starvation during order volume spikes.
recommendedActions.verification: Check order-service configuration repository and observe pool utilization metrics during peak trading or simulated load testing.

recommendedActions.action: Implement dedicated client connection pool metrics and alerting on order-service (e.g. pool saturation percentage, connection wait queue depth).
recommendedActions.rationale: Enables proactive alerting before pool timeouts trigger 503 errors and helps detect client-side bottlenecks immediately.
recommendedActions.verification: Verify new metric dashboards and alert rules trigger during synthetic load testing when pool saturation approaches 80%.

recommendedActions.action: Establish production change validation guidelines requiring peak-volume load simulations before downsizing client pools to align with generic service mesh defaults.
recommendedActions.rationale: CHG-48221 reduced connection limits to match default service mesh values without accounting for high-burst market open order flows.
recommendedActions.verification: Review change management policies and require capacity validation sign-off for critical path trading services.

report.justification: The investigation concluded with conclusive evidence establishing the root cause without requiring additional investigation. The evidence ledger contains explicit log messages identifying the 20/20 client pool exhaustion to broker-connector, matching the configuration change CHG-48221 that lowered max_connections_per_host from 200 to 20 on Friday before market open, alongside metric evidence ruling out broker and database bottlenecks.

findings.summary: Database metrics and logs during 03:15-05:15 UTC confirm that the database was operating normally and experienced no contention, high connection saturation, elevated lock waits, or spike in slow queries at the 03:45 UTC market open. Active connections (175.5), db_lock_wait_ms (~4.0 ms), cpu_utilization (~36%), and slow queries (~4/min) at 03:45 UTC were all completely normal. Database saturation is ruled out as the cause of order processing delays or failures.

observations.statement: Database active_connections remained stable throughout the investigation window (mean 175.8, range 159.7-193.1), with 175.5 connections at 03:45 UTC, showing no connection saturation or spike at market open.
Database db_lock_wait_ms remained consistently low (mean 3.97 ms, range 3.39-4.47 ms), reading 4.03 ms at 03:45 UTC, indicating no lock contention.
Database slow_queries_per_min stayed between 0 and 7 count/min (mean 2.87 count/min) throughout the window, showing 4 count/min at 03:45 UTC with no surge.
Database cpu_utilization remained normal between 33.76% and 40.22% (mean 36.90%), registering 36.11% at 03:45 UTC.
Database request_rate fluctuated normally around 3661-4643 queries/s (mean 4033 queries/s), with 3886 queries/s at 03:45 UTC, exhibiting no abnormal spike.
Database logs recorded no ERROR or FATAL messages between 03:15 UTC and 05:15 UTC, and only 7 isolated slow query warnings across the entire 2-hour window.

The database did not experience contention, high connection saturation, lock waits, or slow query degradation during the 03:45 UTC market open surge, ruling out database saturation as the cause of order-service failures and latency.

# Investigation report: Orders failing at market open again

**Outcome:** conclusive · **Stop reason:** completed · **Confidence:** 0.95 · **Written by:** reporting agent

## Summary
On Monday 2026-09-28 at market open (09:15 IST / 03:45 UTC), stock orders failed at an elevated error rate of ~17.5% across /v1/orders on order-service. While the on-call SRE initially suspected an external broker outage or throttling similar to past incidents PIR-2006 and PIR-2018, investigation of broker-connector showed nominal error rates (<0.4%) and healthy upstream latencies. The failures were directly caused by configuration change CHG-48221 applied on Friday 2026-09-25, which reduced order-service's HTTP client connection pool to broker-connector from 200 to 20 connections per host. During the Monday market open order surge, this client connection pool became fully saturated (20/20 busy), throwing 503 timeouts on 423 order placement requests between 03:45 UTC and 04:19 UTC.

**Root cause:** Configuration change CHG-48221 executed on 2026-09-25T13:00:00Z reduced order-service's broker_client.max_connections_per_host from 200 to 20. During the first subsequent market open surge on Monday 2026-09-28 at 03:45 UTC (09:15 IST), concurrent order volume overwhelmed the constrained 20-connection pool, causing 423 HTTP 503 errors with 'timed out waiting for a connection to broker-connector (client pool 20/20 busy)' until order traffic subsided around 04:19 UTC.

## Hypotheses
1. **Configuration change CHG-48221 reduced order-service's outgoing HTTP client connection pool to broker-connector from 200 to 20, causing connection pool exhaustion and 503 timeouts during the Monday market open order surge.** — `order-service`, config_change, confidence 0.95, supported
   - Supporting: [ev_3, ev_13, ev_15, ev_19, ev_24] · Contradicting: none
   - Directly evidenced by change record CHG-48221 modifying broker_client.max_connections_per_host from 200 to 20, dependency metadata indicating a 20-connection cap, order-service error rate jumping from ~0.4% to ~17.5% at 03:46 UTC, and 423 explicit error logs stating 'timed out waiting for a connection to broker-connector (client pool 20/20 busy)'.
2. **External broker API degradation or rate limiting throttled order placement during the opening auction, mirroring past incidents PIR-2006 and PIR-2018.** — `broker-connector`, rate_limiting_or_quota, confidence 0.05, ruled_out
   - Supporting: [ev_9, ev_10] · Contradicting: [ev_1, ev_3, ev_7, ev_14, ev_15, ev_16, ev_20]
   - broker-connector showed no matching degradation: error rates remained below 0.38%, rate_limited_count was flat at 0-2/min, retry counts peaked at only 8/min, p95 upstream order latency peaked at 218.5 ms, and no order errors were recorded in broker-connector logs.

## Facts
- On Friday 2026-09-25T13:00:00.000Z, configuration change CHG-48221 reduced broker_client.max_connections_per_host on order-service from 200 to 20. [ev_13]
- order-service error_rate surged from baseline (~0.35%-0.5%) to ~17.4%-17.65% beginning at 03:46 UTC (09:16 IST) and remained elevated until returning to baseline at 04:19 UTC. [ev_24]
- Between 2026-09-28T03:45:02Z and 2026-09-28T04:18:59Z, order-service logged 423 status 503 ERROR entries on /v1/orders stating 'order <ref> failed: timed out waiting for a connection to broker-connector (client pool 20/20 busy)'. [ev_3, ev_15]
- broker-connector error rate remained under 0.38% (mean 0.21%), rate_limited_count averaged 0.225/min (max 2/min), retry_count peaked at 8/min, and p95 upstream latency on orders peaked at 218.5 ms. [ev_1, ev_7, ev_14, ev_16]
- order-service database pool wait time peaked at 5.57 ms (mean 3.03 ms) and CPU utilization peaked at 65.97% at 03:45 UTC, remaining below saturation. [ev_17, ev_23]
- Database metrics showed active connections of ~175.5, lock wait times under 4.5 ms, slow queries under 7/min, and CPU utilization of ~36% around 03:45 UTC. [ev_2, ev_4, ev_5, ev_6, ev_11, ev_12]

## Inferences
- Market open on Monday 2026-09-28 at 09:15 IST (03:45 UTC) was the first high-concurrency order placement burst experienced by order-service since connection limits were reduced tenfold by CHG-48221 on Friday after market close. [ev_13, ev_15, ev_24]
- The reporter's hypothesis of an external broker API outage or throttling (PIR-2006 / PIR-2018) was disproven by broker-connector's healthy upstream metrics and logs. [ev_1, ev_7, ev_14, ev_16, ev_20]
- Internal order-service resources (CPU and database connections) and database infrastructure were not bottlenecked; failures were exclusively caused by client pool starvation between order-service and broker-connector. [ev_3, ev_15, ev_17, ev_21, ev_23]

## Assumptions
- Normal market open trading volume on Monday mornings requires significantly more than 20 concurrent downstream connections to broker-connector to handle order concurrency without queue timeouts.
